# Shell completion is generated by reactor, not hand-written per shell

`reactor completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a completion script for that shell.
`scripts/install.py` installs all three, unconditionally, into the
conventional per-user location for each. The scripts themselves are thin: the
static part (subcommands, flags) is a small case statement per shell, and the
dynamic part (tool ids, toolset ids) shells back into a new hidden command,
`reactor __complete tools|toolsets`, which prints bare newline-separated ids
with no probing.

## Why

**The command surface already lives in one place, and completion is a second
copy of it.** `build_parser()` in `bin/reactor` is the actual set of
subcommands and flags. A hand-maintained `completions/reactor.bash` (and its
zsh and fish siblings) is a second, independent statement of the same tree,
written in three languages that cannot check each other. It starts correct and
drifts the first time a subcommand grows a flag and nobody updates three unrelated
files — the same failure mode [ADR-0003](0003-tools-toml-single-source-of-truth.md)
exists to prevent for the catalogue, one level up the stack. Generating the
static case-statement content by hand from `build_parser()`'s current shape,
at the point this was written, is a one-time transcription rather than an
ongoing duplication — the tree is small and changes rarely enough that a
runtime-introspecting generator would be more machinery than the problem
warrants, but the *source of truth* for what ships is still `bin/reactor`, and
the completion scripts must be re-generated by hand whenever a subcommand or
flag changes rather than treated as independently maintainable.

**The dynamic part cannot be static text.** Tool ids and toolset ids come from
`tools.toml`/`toolsets.toml`, which only `reactor` parses
([ADR-0005](0005-reactor-cli-stdlib-python.md)) — a completion script has no
business embedding a TOML reader in bash, zsh, and fish to read them itself.
It has to shell back into `reactor`.

**Completion must be instant, so the query it shells out to must not probe.**
`reactor tools list` detects whether each tool is actually present, which costs
a subprocess even when cached. A `<TAB>` press doesn't need that — it needs
the list of ids the catalogue declares, nothing about the machine. `reactor
__complete tools` loads the catalogue and prints its keys; no probe, no cache
touch, no network. This is a new, deliberately narrow, internal command: it
sits outside the `--format json` contract (ADR-0005's line 13) because its only
consumer is the shipped completion scripts, not an extension or a human, and it
is versioned together with them.

**`reactor completion <shell>` is the idiom users already have muscle memory
for.** kubectl, gh, docker, and rustup all expose the same shape
(`source <(tool completion bash)`), so this costs nothing to explain.

**Installing all three unconditionally is simpler and more correct than
guessing.** `shutil.which("zsh")` tells you a zsh binary exists on this
machine, not that it is anyone's login shell or that its user runs
`compinit`. Three small text files cost nothing to write and nothing to load
if unused, so `scripts/install.py` writes bash's, zsh's, and fish's completion
files every run, the same way it already seeds config unconditionally.

## Consequences

- **A new internal command**, `reactor __complete <tools|toolsets>`, ships
  alongside the completion scripts as one unit — a change to one without the
  other breaks completion silently until the next reinstall. It is deliberately
  left out of `--help` (`help=argparse.SUPPRESS`) so it does not read as a
  fourth documented output contract next to text/json.
- **`scripts/install.py` grows a "completions" step** and a `--no-completions`
  flag, mirroring `--no-skills`. Like skill fetching, a failure here is a
  warning, never fatal — a machine with no `~/.local/share` writable is still a
  working REactor install.
- **zsh needs one manual step the script cannot do for the user**: adding
  `fpath+=(~/.zfunc)` before `compinit` in `.zshrc`, if it is not there
  already. `scripts/install.py` prints this once, the same way rustup and
  pyenv's installers do, rather than editing `.zshrc` itself — editing a
  user's shell rc file unprompted is a worse failure mode than one extra line
  of output.
- **The completion scripts are re-derived by hand**, not generated by a script
  in this repo, whenever `build_parser()`'s subcommands or flags change. There
  is no automated check that they still match; this is the cost of not pulling
  in an introspection dependency (see below), accepted because the surface is
  small and changes rarely.

## Considered and rejected

- **Hand-maintained static files under `completions/`, installed as-is.**
  Rejected: this is the drift failure described above, and it is the design
  that looks like it works right up until the first missed update.
- **Generate completions from argparse introspection at runtime**, e.g. via
  `argcomplete`. Rejected on [ADR-0005](0005-reactor-cli-stdlib-python.md):
  `argcomplete` is not stdlib, and pulling in a dependency for this is the
  exact tradeoff that ADR exists to refuse. It would also still need
  reactor-specific logic bolted on for tool/toolset ids, since argparse has no
  notion of "values live in a TOML catalogue."
- **Have the completion scripts parse `reactor tools list --format json`
  directly**, with an embedded `python3 -c` or `jq`. Rejected: `tools list`
  probes every catalogued tool by default, which is far more work than
  completion needs and makes every `<TAB>` press pay for machine detection;
  `jq` is also not guaranteed present, which shelling into reactor's own
  Python avoids entirely.
- **Auto-detect installed shells and only write matching completions.**
  Rejected: a `which` check answers "is a binary on PATH", not "does this
  person use this shell's completion", and guessing wrong costs nothing to
  avoid by simply writing all three.
